text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of doing everything at once, teams use iterative development, breaking the work into small cycles called sprints. Each sprint typically lasts two to four weeks. Before a sprint begins, the team looks at their backlog, which is a list of all the tasks and features that need to be completed. They select the most important items to work on. These items are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from the perspective of the end user. Every day, the team holds short standup meetings to discuss progress, plan the day, and identify any obstacles. This constant feedback and adjustment help the team deliver value quickly and respond well to changes.
